stem: The number 30 is added to the data set. What is the median of the new data set?
stimulus:
A textile historian records the number of threads per centimetre in five surviving linen fragments:

6, 8, 3, 8, 5
explanation: Sort the six values: 3, 5, 6, 8, 8, 30. With an even count, the median is the mean of the two middle values: (6 + 8) / 2 = 7. The extreme value 30 moves the median by only half a position, from 6 to 7, while the mean jumps from 6 to 10. You will use this check on exam questions that ask what happens to the mean and median when an outlier is added.

A.why: You took the two middle values of the list as written, 3 and 8, without sorting it first. A median always needs the data sorted.

B.why: 6 is the median before 30 was added. With six values the middle is now between two numbers, so you have to recompute it.

D.why: 10 is the new mean, 60 / 6. You assumed the median moves as far as the mean, but an outlier pulls the mean hard and barely shifts the median.

stem: The value 40 is added to the data set. Which statement describes what happens to the mean and the median?
stimulus:
The depths, in kilometres, of seven small earthquakes are:

2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7
choices: The mean increases a lot; the median increases slightly.
The mean and the median increase by the same amount.
The mean increases; the median does not change at all.
The mean does not change; the median increases slightly.
explanation: The mean goes from 30/7 ≈ 4.3 to 70/8 = 8.75, a large jump toward 40. The median goes from 4 (the 4th of 7 values) to (4 + 5)/2 = 4.5, only half a position. An extreme value drags the mean and barely moves the median. Exam questions about adding an outlier test exactly this.

B.why: This is the trap. You assumed the median shifts as much as the mean, but the median moves by at most one position no matter how large the new value is.

C.why: With 8 values the median becomes the average of the 4th and 5th values, 4 and 5, so it does change slightly. You have to check whether the middle actually moves.

D.why: You reversed the roles. The mean is the measure that the extreme value pulls hard, so it cannot stay the same.

stem: Which statement can be determined from this summary alone?
stimulus:
Load test results for 15 bridge deck panels, in tonnes, are summarised as a box plot would show them.

Five-Number Summary of Panel Loads (tonnes)
Minimum | Q1 | Median | Q3 | Maximum
10 | 14 | 18 | 22 | 40
explanation: A box plot, or its five-number summary, shows the median directly. Here it is 18. The plot does not show the mean, because the same five numbers fit many data sets with different means. On exam questions that compare box plots, any claim about a mean cannot be 'must be true'.

B.why: This is the trap. You read the median line as if it showed the mean. A box plot never tells you the mean.

C.why: You averaged the five summary numbers: 104 / 5 = 20.8. Those are markers, not the 15 data values, so their average is not the mean of the data.

D.why: 25 is halfway between the minimum and the maximum, (10 + 40) / 2. That is the midrange, not the median. The median is the line inside the box.

stem: What is the mean daily rainfall for these days?
stimulus:
A hydrologist records the daily rainfall at one gauge over 13 days.

Daily Rainfall at Gauge 4
Rainfall (cm) | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6
Number of days | 1 | 3 | 5 | 3 | 1
explanation: The frequencies 1, 3, 5, 3, 1 are symmetric around 4 cm, so the mean is the centre of symmetry, 4. To check: (2 + 9 + 20 + 15 + 6) / 13 = 52 / 13 = 4. In Desmos, mean([2,3,4,5,6],[1,3,5,3,1]) gives the same result. The exam uses this to have you rank several tables by mean: the symmetric ones sit at their centre, and you look at which way the non-symmetric one leans.

A.why: You averaged the frequencies: 13 / 5 = 2.6. The mean is about the rainfall values, weighted by how many days each one occurred.

C.why: 5 is the frequency in the middle column, the number of days with 4 cm. You read a count as a rainfall value.

D.why: 13 is the total number of days, which is the denominator. You stopped before dividing the weighted total by it.
